investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-08T18:48–18:56Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to remain absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity selector. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints at all. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request is immediately stuck Unschedulable, preventing VM provisioning from starting and leaving all required eval evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) uncollected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; the pod scheduling failure occurs before this call can return, so no evidence is ever written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: both nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity selector have consumed their full kata.peerpods.io/vm quota, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or label drift: the four remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, which may indicate a cluster topology change (node replacement, label removal, or taint addition) that reduced the eligible node pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes, amplifying the capacity pressure.

Tertiary — leaked or stuck remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: previously created remote-agent pods that were not cleaned up may be holding the vm resource allocation on the two eligible nodes, preventing new pods from scheduling.

Lower confidence — eval runner cleanup (withCleanup) not releasing VM resources from prior runs: if a previous eval run failed mid-cleanup, residual VM allocations could be occupying the limited kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval succeeds and returns vmIdPresent=true with a valid remoteState, the capacity exhaustion was transient and has since resolved.

If kubectl or equivalent tooling shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available on the two affinity-eligible nodes, the scheduling failure has a different cause (e.g., a quota admission webhook or a node condition other than resource pressure).

If the two affinity-eligible nodes show no running pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the resource exhaustion diagnosis is incorrect and the cause may be a node condition, taint, or scheduler plugin misconfiguration.

If the four non-affinity-matching nodes are found to have the correct labels and the pod spec's affinity selector is the element that changed, the primary cause shifts to a pod spec or node label regression rather than capacity exhaustion.

If no-history data (previousRunCount=0, lastPassingAt=null) is explained by a brand-new eval rather than a regression, the failure may represent an environment that has never had sufficient capacity for this eval, not a capacity regression.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on affinity-eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure check rather than a timeout.

Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 nodes with available vm slots), alerting before all capacity is consumed.

Add a leaked-vm-cleanup eval that counts non-terminal remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found, catching withCleanup regressions before they exhaust scheduling capacity.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and record the Kubernetes scheduling error message as a structured evidence field (e.g., schedulingError), so future failures surface the exact constraint in the evidence object rather than only in the check message.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-08T18:51–18:56Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote agent swarm has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates that the two peer-pod-capable nodes are fully consumed and preemption cannot free capacity. As a result, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returns a live agent, the probe exits before writing any evidence, and all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) remain missing. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905 (lines 1904-1905): runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent(..., 'remote', ...) — the pod scheduling failure occurs inside createAgent before any evidence can be written.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266 (line 264): contract requires [orgId, agentId, readyState, state] — none present because agent creation never completed.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two peer-pod-capable nodes: both nodes are fully allocated, no preemption victims exist, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. This directly matches the scheduler message in failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

SECONDARY — Insufficient peer-pod-capable node count: only 2 of 6 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource. If concurrent eval runs or live workloads consumed those slots before the eval pod was submitted, the eval would fail even if per-node capacity is not permanently exhausted.

TERTIARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 nodes: the pod's scheduling constraints exclude 4 nodes entirely, reducing the effective scheduling domain to 2 nodes. A misconfigured or overly restrictive affinity rule could be contributing to the bottleneck.
LOWER CONFIDENCE — Transient spike in remote agent workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the eval run, which may self-resolve without infrastructure changes.

Kubernetes node inspection showing that kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are not actually exhausted (i.e., allocatable > requested on both peer-pod nodes) would suggest the scheduler message was caused by a different constraint such as a quota, admission webhook, or runtime class misconfiguration rather than raw resource exhaustion.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-08T18:48–18:56Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to remain absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity selector. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints at all. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request is immediately stuck Unschedulable, preventing VM provisioning from starting and leaving all required eval evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) uncollected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: both nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity selector have consumed their full kata.peerpods.io/vm quota, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or label drift: the four remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, which may indicate a cluster topology change (node replacement, label removal, or taint addition) that reduced the eligible node pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes, amplifying the capacity pressure.

Tertiary — leaked or stuck remote-agent VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: previously created remote-agent pods that were not cleaned up may be holding the vm resource allocation on the two eligible nodes, preventing new pods from scheduling.

Lower confidence — eval runner cleanup (withCleanup) not releasing VM resources from prior runs: if a previous eval run failed mid-cleanup, residual VM allocations could be occupying the limited kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on affinity-eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure check rather than a timeout.

Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity selector meets a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 nodes with available vm slots), alerting before all capacity is consumed.

Add a leaked-vm-cleanup eval that counts non-terminal remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found, catching withCleanup regressions before they exhaust scheduling capacity.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to capture and record the Kubernetes scheduling error message as a structured evidence field (e.g., schedulingError), so future failures surface the exact constraint in the evidence object rather than only in the check message.

The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates that the two peer-pod-capable nodes are fully consumed and preemption cannot free capacity. As a result, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returns a live agent, the probe exits before writing any evidence, and all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) remain missing. possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots on the nodes that satisfy the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector are currently consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector rules, meaning the schedulable pool is effectively limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size. If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their labels changed, the effective capacity would drop to zero.
Tertiary — resource quota or limit range at the namespace level preventing new kata peer-pod VMs from being allocated even if node capacity existed.
Lower probability — a transient spike in concurrent remote agent workloads temporarily exhausted VM slots; if the spike subsides the checks may self-recover without intervention.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields, it would indicate the scheduling failure was a transient capacity spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If kubectl (or equivalent) shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and unused on the 2 affinity-matching nodes, the root cause would shift to a pod spec misconfiguration or API-level rejection rather than resource exhaustion.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have the correct labels and the pod affinity/selector rules are confirmed unchanged, the diagnosis of affinity/selector drift would be disproved and the cause would be isolated purely to VM slot exhaustion on the 2 matching nodes.

If a different check in the remote-agents feature (e.g., a hypothetical health-ping that does not require pod scheduling) passed during the same window, it would confirm the failure is scoped to pod scheduling rather than a broader API or network outage.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type exists on any node in the cluster, the failure would indicate a missing node plugin or resource registration rather than exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on the affinity-matching nodes, alerting before slots are fully exhausted rather than only after pod scheduling fails.
Add a node-affinity-health eval that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote agent pod's affinity/selector rules, catching label drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.

Add a scheduling-latency eval that warns when remote agent pod scheduling latency exceeds a threshold (e.g., 30s) well before the 144s Unschedulable timeout, enabling earlier detection of capacity pressure.
Consider a canary eval that attempts to schedule a minimal remote agent pod on a fixed cadence and reports scheduling success/failure and latency as a leading indicator of VM slot availability.
